question.text: At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>363</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>, the vapour pressure of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>21</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kPa</mi></math> and that of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>18</mn><mi>kPa</mi></math>. One mole of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> moles of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> are mixed. Assuming that this solution is ideal, the vapour pressure of the mixture is___________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kPa</mi></math>. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo></math>Round of to the Nearest Integer<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>)</mo></math>.

solution.text:
Given PA0=21 kPa  ⇒PB0=18 kPa

→ An Ideal solution is prepared by mixing 1 mole A and 2 mole B.

→XA=13 and XB=23

→ According to Raoult's law

PT=XAPA0+XBPB0

⇒  PT=13×21+23×18

⇒  PT=7+12=19 kPa
